data.body:
R3 dry-run enumeration RE-RUN on origin/main @ 0b851c8103 (2026-08-19), both blockers now CLOSED (fea4-f98c bridge-state writes; 6454-d06e binding-store/alert_store parity). Result: TWO out-of-transaction composition sites remain, BOTH with a durable reason — not remediation debt.

SITE 1 — src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (_commit_binding_store_snapshot: git_adapter.add + git_adapter.commit). Blocker 6454-d06e was originally scoped to convert this and DID NOT: its closed description carries a 'Scope note — binding-snapshot conversion was ATTEMPTED and REVERTED (behavior-preserving boundary)'. Evidence recorded there: routing it through push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch (the only offered commit seam, which stages with 'git add -A') sweeps in .bridge_state/last-pass.json, which the deliberate selective 5-file staging excludes, so the tickets HEAD advances on every idempotent pass and tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head goes RED (reproduced in CI on change 1821 ps1 and locally). Preserving the exact committed set through the seam needs EITHER a seam pathspec parameter OR a write_lock-wrapped selective-commit helper — both descoped. DISPOSITION: durable reasoned inline marker citing that boundary, plus a discovered_from follow-up ticket owning the seam-pathspec gap so the debt is visible in the tracker, not only in-tree.

SITE 2 — src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:338-351 (_purge_committed_reconciler_locks: read_tree/rm_cached/write_tree/commit_tree/update_ref). Confirmed on the current tree exactly as the earlier dry-run described: a DETACHED temp index (GIT_INDEX_FILE=<repo>/.git/reconciler-purge-index) plus a CAS ref-advance (update_ref with old_value). It never touches the worktree or the main index, and the CAS is the concurrency control. DISPOSITION: durable reasoned inline marker. Rejected the alternative 'exempt detached-index operations as a rule' — GIT_INDEX_FILE arrives as an env dict built at the call site, so detachedness is not statically decidable from the callable alone, and a blanket rule would be trivially forgeable by any future caller passing env=; a per-site reasoned marker keeps the sanction explicit and auditable. Rejected 'promote into git_adapter as a named transaction helper' — one caller, legacy migration slated for deletion; a new seam export would outlive its only use.

ALSO CORRECTED from the plan text: commit_email is NOT a mutation primitive. git_adapter.commit_email is 'git log -1 --format=%ae' — a READ despite the name. Including it in R3's primitive set would be a false-positive generator. R3's mutation set is add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree.
